learning_outcomes.text: Know and apply the fundamentals of descriptive statistics to describe data sets similar to those resulting from problems in the industrial area.
Know and apply the principles of probability to solving problems similar to those arising in engineering.
Is able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions, and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.
Apply basic knowledge of regression and correlation, sampling, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, and multivariate analysis to problems related to industrial engineering.
Is able to use statistical software to design and solve statistical problems in real environments related to industrial engineering.

teaching_methods: Presentation of concepts and problem-solving in the classroom, including discussion classes and common sharing.
Laboratory activities of increasing difficulty for autonomous problem-solving.
Completion of work in small groups.
Personal study, report writing, practical work as independent student work.

assessment_methods.method: Completed activities/courses (including laboratory practical development reports, problem solving, group work, report writing, presentation and defense of practical cases or projects)

assessment_rules: To pass by continuous assessment, students must score 5 or higher in both theoretical-practical written tests, complete established activities, and attend over 70% of classes. If these conditions are met, the final grade is 40% from each written test and 20% from completed activities. If conditions are not met, the final grade is 60% from the final written exam, 20% from written tests, and 20% from completed activities. The final exam grade prevails if higher. In the extraordinary call, only the final exam grade is considered.
